docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
GigaMeter Research Hub

The open-source telemetry research on internet connectivity, network quality, and physical location integrity across GigaMeter installed public facilities.

Spatial Intelligence

Models for entity geofencing, hardware mobility trajectories, and Wi-Fi spatial clustering.

Connectivity & Outages

Advanced telemetry models evaluating network uptime.

Network Diagnostics

docs.title: src.facility_validator.FacilityValidator
docs.text:
Two-Track Facility Location Truth & Validation Engine for GigaMeter Telemetry.

Location Truth (Pillar 3)

Evaluates building location against official government records using the unpenalized spatial confidence of the primary cluster.

Hardware Integrity (Pillars 1 & 2)

Evaluates device reliability, detects mobile hotspots and spatial splits (> 2km), and applies the multiplicative BSSID Coherence Penalty (P_coherence).

docs.title: run_national_facility_audit(force_refresh=False)
docs.text: Runs the Two-Track validation engine across all facilities in the dataset. Results are cached in self._national_audit_cache to avoid redundant multi-pass calculations. Set force_refresh=True to clear and re-execute the audit.

docs.title: Geofencing: Technical Blueprint & Research Methodology
docs.text:
Version: v0.2

Status: Hardening (exploring edge cases)

Maturity: Active Baseline

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text: The primary objective of this framework is to replace static, self-reported administrative registries with spatially verified, crowdsourced field telemetry. By capturing background Wi-Fi BSSID environmental scans and high-frequency active speedtests via the GigaMeter application, the system dynamically calculates location truth, evaluates device mobility trajectories, and cross-validates official government administrative records.

docs.title: 1.1 The 3 Research Pillars Fall Under This Topis
docs.text: Pillar Name Primary Input Data Core Methodologies Primary Output / Operational Value Pillar 1: Entity Geofencing & Mobility Time-series coordinates, device_id, timestamps DBSCAN clustering (eps=150m), operational window (08:00–19:59) Mobility classification (STATIONARY, COMMUTER, RELOCATED, HIGH_MOBILITY). Pillar 2: Geolocation Quality & Confidence Google API resolved lat/lon, accuracy, BSSIDs, SSIDs Inverse-variance weighted centroids, 5-factor scoring model, BSSID Coherence Penalty Unpenalized location score (S_raw​), mobile hotspot tags, hardware health score. Pillar 3: Government Data Validation Empirical facility centroids, official government registry pins Haversine displacement (D_govt​), Two-Track Engine Architecture Decoupled location verification flags (VERIFIED_ACCURATE, GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH, etc.).

docs.title: 1.2 The Two-Track Engine Paradigm Shift
docs.text:
Earlier iterations of spatial validation utilized a single-flag cascade where severe hardware volatility (e.g., a laptop transported 200km between a school and a regional office) or high mobile hotspot usage forced the system into outputting a single flag such as BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT. This created an analytical paradox: even if the primary spatial cluster matched the official government registry pin perfectly (<= 30m), the single-flag system masked the verified physical building location under a hardware anomaly tag.

To eliminate this paradox, v0.2 introduces the Two-Track Engine Architecture, cleanly decoupling two independent research dimensions:

  1. Track 1: Location Truth Engine (Pillar 3 Focus): Evaluates the physical location of the brick-and-mortar facility against official government administrative records using the unpenalized spatial confidence score (S_raw, 0–100) of the primary empirical cluster.
  2. Track 2: Hardware Integrity Engine (Pillars 1 & 2 Focus): Evaluates device deployment permanence, mobile hotspot dependency, and spatial split anomalies (> 2km), applying a multiplicative BSSID Coherence Penalty (P_coherence) to yield a dedicated hardware_health_score and decoupled hardware_anomaly_tags.

docs.title: 2.1 Overview & Pillar Integration Mechanics
docs.text:
Raw crowdsourced telemetry contains significant spatial noise introduced by personal mobile tethering (teacher smartphones), staff commuter devices, and hardware relocations. To transform raw Wi-Fi BSSID environmental scans into an empirical location truth engine, processing is organised into a 4-Layer Consolidation Framework.

This 4-layer model directly operationalises our core research pillars: * Layer 1 executes Pillar 1 (MobilityAnalyzer) to isolate device-level mobility trajectories and extract primary operational clusters. * Layer 2 executes Pillar 2 (SpatialProfiler) to calculate accuracy-weighted empirical centroids across persistent fixed infrastructure. * Layer 3 executes the composite scoring engine inside FacilityValidator to measure hardware stability, multi-device spatial consensus, and BSSID coherence. * Layer 4 completes Pillars 1, 2 & 3 (FacilityValidator) by cross-validating empirical centroids against official government administrative coordinates to output decoupled primary location flags and secondary hardware anomaly tags.

docs.text:
graph TD

  1. SpatialProfiler answers: "Where is the physical building located?"

  2. MobilityAnalyzer answers: "How are the individual devices moving relative to that building?"

  3. FacilityValidator answers: "Can we verify the building location on government maps (Track 1), and how reliable is the installed monitoring hardware (Track 2)?"

docs.title: 3.1 Overview & Trajectory Disambiguation
docs.text: The MobilityAnalyzer module evaluates hardware movement trajectories at the individual device_id level. It utilizes DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) with a native Haversine metric to group geographic locations into spatial clusters without requiring a pre-defined cluster count.

docs.title: Processing Passes:
docs.text:
• Pass 1: Mobile Hotspot & Drift Filtering: Identifies personal mobile hotspots and tags high-volatility BSSIDs to prevent consumer phones from skewing hardware trajectory analysis.
  • Pass 2: Density-Based Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN): Groups valid coordinate pairs per device using a spatial radius threshold (eps = 150 meters) and a minimum density threshold (min_samples = 3).
  • Pass 3: Temporal & Operational Disambiguation: Evaluates scan distributions across clusters during active operational hours (08:00–19:59) vs. off-hours/weekends.
  • Pass 4: Behavioral Classification & Geofence Auditing: Classifies hardware behavior into four operational states: STATIONARY, COMMUTER, RELOCATED, or HIGH_MOBILITY.

docs.text: Mobility Class Cluster Count (K) Spatial Pattern Temporal Behavior Real-World Operational Context STATIONARY 1 Primary Cluster Tight spatial anchor (<=150m - 200m) High compliance (>= 90%) across all days and hours Dedicated, fixed desktop or router monitoring hardware anchored to the school building. COMMUTER 2+ Clusters Alternates between Cluster 0 (School) and Cluster 1+ (Home/Off-site) Cluster 0 during active hours (08:00–19:59); Cluster 1 off-hours and weekends Mobile laptop or tablet owned by a teacher/staff member who brings it to work and takes it home. docs.title: 4.1 Overview & Data Ingestion Rules
docs.text: The SpatialProfiler module serves as the foundational spatial processing engine. It ingests raw telemetry measurements, standardizes facility identifiers (school_id_giga), enriches records with local device timestamps, and tags consumer mobile hotspots, and resolves empirical facility centroids using configurable strategy modes.

docs.title: Processing Rules:
docs.text:
1. Strict No-IP Fallback Policy: The profiler strictly discards records where detected_latitude or detected_longitude is null. IP-based geolocation fallback is never applied.
  2. Operational Window Isolation: Time-series telemetry is filtered strictly between 08:00:00 and 19:59:59 local device time (is_operational_hours = True) to prevent nighttime or off-hour device transport from skewing facility locations.
  3. Consumer Hotspot & Drift Engine:
    1. SSID Regex Pattern Matching: Passive and active SSIDs are evaluated against a consumer hotspot pattern:
      1. Pattern = (?i)(iphone\android\galaxy\hotspot\teacher\pixel\redmi\tether\samsung\huawei\oppo\vivo\xiaomi\realme\mobicom\unitel\mifi)
    2. Multi-Day Spatial Drift Check: BSSIDs displaying multi-day spatial drift exceeding 1000m across different dates are tagged as is_hotspot_drift = True.
  4. Candidate BSSID Spatial Clustering & Spatial Splits:
    • Pairwise distances (D_bssid) between BSSID centroids are calculated.
    • D_bssid <= 200m → Merged & averaged (same physical campus/building).
    • 200m < D_bssid \<= 2000m → Retained as minor campus dispersion.
    • D_bssid > 2000m → Triggers BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT anomaly tag.

docs.title: 4.2 Configurable Primary Cluster Resolution Strategies
docs.text:
To address BSSID splits (> 2km) without introducing analytical bias, SpatialProfiler supports three configurable resolution modes:

  • Mode 1: GOVT_PROXIMITY_ANCHOR (Prior-Informed Default): If a BSSID split occurs, the engine checks if any candidate cluster centroid is <= 2000m from official government coordinates (phi_govt, lambda_govt). If candidate clusters exist near the government pin, it selects the cluster with the highest operational scan density among them.

  • Mode 2: TELEMETRY_DOMINANCE (Unbiased Field Benchmark): Evaluates spatial data strictly based on scan volume during active operational hours (08:00–19:59), ignoring government coordinates entirely. Ideal for Pillar 3 auditing without circular reasoning.

  • Mode 3: STATIONARY_FIRST (Hardware-First Mode): Filters candidate clusters for scans originating strictly from devices classified as STATIONARY before computing the facility centroid.

docs.title: 5.1 Overview & Two-Track Engine Logic
docs.text: The FacilityValidator module consolidates multi-device spatial clusters into a Two-Track Validation Engine. It bridges empirical field telemetry with administrative metadata to evaluate two independent tracks: Location Truth (Pillar 3) and Hardware Health (Pillars 1 & 2).

docs.title: 5.2 Comprehensive 5-Factor Score Component Breakdown
docs.text:
The raw spatial confidence score (S_raw, 0–100) evaluates five distinct spatial and operational dimensions of the primary empirical cluster:

\[S_{\text{raw}} = S_{\text{stability}} + S_{\text{consensus}} + S_{\text{bssid}} + S_{\text{depth}} + S_{\text{precision}}\] Component Name Max Points Tracked Inputs & Metrics Mathematical Logic & Evaluation Rules Operational Impact & Thresholds 1. Device Stability Profile (S_stability) 30 pts Categorical mobility class of all devices registered to facility (STATIONARY, COMMUTER, RELOCATED, HIGH_MOBILITY). if STATIONARY in devices: score = 30.0elif COMMUTER in devices: score = 20.0else: score = 10.0 Evaluates hardware permanence. Awarded 30 points if at least one stationary device anchors the building. 2. Multi-Device Spatial Consensus (S_consensus) 25 pts Maximum pairwise Haversine distance (d_max in meters) between primary cluster centroids across multiple devices. if d_max <= 30: score = 25.0elif 30 < d_max <= 200:score = 25.0 * (1.0 - (d_max - 30) / 170.0)else: score = 0.0(Single-device default = 12.5 pts) Evaluates whether distinct hardware devices agree on facility location. d_max > 200m indicates conflicting hardware setups. 3. BSSID Infrastructure Persistence (S_bssid) 20 pts Presence of fixed, non-null BSSIDs and active operational days recorded with valid BSSIDs. if bssid_exists and days_active >= 3:score = 20.0else: score = 10.0 Rewards persistent Wi-Fi router infrastructure. Ambient background scans without associated BSSIDs receive 10 points. 4. Data Temporal Depth (S_depth) 15 pts Count of unique operational days recorded in the observation window. score = min(15.0, 15.0 * (days_active / 10.0)) Scales linearly up to 10 active days. Reaching 10+ operational days awards the full 15 points. 5. API Precision Radius (S_precision) 10 pts Mean reported Google Geolocation API accuracy radius (mean_acc in meters). score = max(0.0, 10.0 * (1.0 - (mean_acc - 10) / 90.0)) Evaluates precision returned by Google API. mean_acc <= 10m receives 10 points; mean_acc >= 100m receives 0 points.

docs.title: 5.3 BSSID Coherence Penalty Factor (P_coherence)
docs.text:
The BSSID Coherence Penalty measures spatial agreement across all BSSIDs associated with a facility (D_bssid_max in meters). It is applied strictly to Track 2 (Hardware Health) to penalize roaming hardware without degrading Track 1 (Location Truth):

\[P_{\text{coherence}} = \begin{cases} 1.0, & \text{if } D_{\text{bssid_max}} \le 1000\text{m } \text{(Tight Alignment)} \\[1ex] 1.0 - 0.5 \times \left( \frac{D_{\text{bssid_max}} - 1000}{1000} \right), & \text{if } 1000\text{m} < D_{\text{bssid_max}} \le 2000\text{m} \\[1ex] 0.1, & \text{if } D_{\text{bssid_max}} > 2000\text{m } \text{(Severe BSSID Split)} \end{cases}\] \[\text{Track 1 (Location Confidence Score)} = S_{\text{raw}}\] \[\text{Track 2 (Hardware Health Score)} = S_{\text{raw}} \times P_{\text{coherence}}\]

docs.title: 7.1 Track 1: Primary Location Verification Flags (Pillar 3)
docs.text: Location Flag Trigger Conditions Real-World Operational Interpretation Recommended Action VERIFIED_ACCURATE S_raw >= 70.0 AND D_govt <= 200m Field telemetry confirms official government registry coordinates. High-confidence baseline established. None. Facility baseline verified. GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH S_raw >= 70.0 AND D_govt > 500m Empirical telemetry is spatially stable, but government coordinates are significantly inaccurate (e.g., pinned to village center or district office). Submit spatial coordinate correction to Ministry. CAMPUS_DISPERSION S_raw >= 60.0 AND 200m < D_govt <= 500m Telemetry confirms presence near the government pin, but spatial spread reflects a large multi-building campus, sports field, or peripheral annex. Retain location as valid; flag for minor boundary refinement. UNSTABLE_MOBILE_ONLY S_raw < 50.0 Telemetry is too sparse or spatially volatile to guarantee physical building coordinates. Needs fixed monitoring hardware. NO_GOVT_PIN_AVAILABLE Official Govt Coordinates missing/null Empirical centroid calculated successfully, but no government metadata exists for comparison. Append empirical centroid to registry. INSUFFICIENT_DATA Total valid spatial scans < 5 in the observation window Fewer than 5 valid spatial scans recorded in the observation window. Await additional telemetry syncs.

docs.title: 7.2 Track 2: Secondary Hardware Anomaly Tags (Pillars 1 & 2)
docs.text: Anomaly Tag Trigger Conditions Real-World Operational Interpretation Recommended Action BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT Max pairwise BSSID distance D_bssid_max > 2000m (2km) Hardware monitoring devices registered to this facility operate across two or more distinct geographic locations (e.g., laptop transported between school and regional office). Flag monitoring setup as mobile. Dedicated fixed hardware missing at the school. HOTSPOT_TETHERED_FACILITY Active Wi-Fi scans matching consumer hotspot patterns or multi-day drift > 1km are >= 50% Entity relies primarily on staff personal smartphones or mobile hotspots for connectivity rather than fixed ISP infrastructure. Flag connectivity as temporary/mobile tethered. Exclude mobile SSIDs from building checks.

docs.title: 8. Summary of Research Data Dictionary Rules
docs.text:
• Measurement Source Filtering: Raw measurement payloads use source = 'DailyCheckApp' in the database. Data is filtered on this field for app-specific speedtest analysis.
  • Timezone Standardization: Raw UTC timestamps (created_timestamp) always converted to local device time before executing operational hour (08:00–19:59) models.
  • Strict No-IP Fallback Policy: IP-based geolocation is never used by GigaMeter. Always filter out null coordinates (WHERE detected_latitude IS NOT NULL) before spatial calculations. IP fallback imputation NEVER been attempted.

docs.title: Pillar 4: Outage Classification, Connectivity Modeling & 4-State Telemetry
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
Determining whether an entity is "online" or "offline" is a non-trivial challenge. A missing telemetry record or failed ping does not automatically indicate an Internet Service Provider (ISP) network blackout.

Real-world deployment environments introduce significant non-network variables:

  1. Facility Operational Schedules: Schools and public facilities close at night and on weekends; hardware is powered off.

  2. Power Grid Instability: Local power grids experience blackouts, shutting down both client hardware and local routers simultaneously.

  3. Offline Sync & Caching Engine: The GigaMeter application utilizes local browser storage (IndexedDB) to cache telemetry offline during outages:

    • Ping Telemetry: Written to IndexedDB immediately upon generation and synced to the server via a background job every 2 hours.
    • Active Speedtests: Measurement payloads are cached locally and synced automatically once connectivity is re-established (retaining up to 7 days of history).
    • Data Retention Rules: Local synced telemetry rows are pruned after 3 days, while un-synced historical data is purged after 30 days.

Pillar 4 exists to establish a rigorous, deterministic baseline for entity connectivity during active operational hours (08:00–19:59 local device time) and serve as the foundation for predictive modeling and automated disconnection alarms.

docs.title: 2. Deterministic Starting Baseline: The 4-State Taxonomy
docs.text:
Time-series ping telemetry (generated every 15 minutes during operational hours) is deterministically categorized into four analytical states:

State Status Name Logical Database Conditions Analytical Interpretation & Real-World Context Metric Impact State A Internet ON is_connected = TRUEAND latency is numerical Client device active, app container functional, end-to-end network reachability validated. Uptime Numerator & Denominator State B Internet OFF is_connected = FALSE Client active, WAN reachability explicitly failed. (Cached in IndexedDB locally; may sync up to 2 hours late). Downtime Denominator State D Degraded / Discrepancy is_connected = TRUEAND latency IS NULL Widespread global pattern (~6.50% of dataset): Connection check succeeds, but latency returns null (severe packet loss or async promise boundary timeout). Awaiting final engineering clarification; isolated in sensitivity models. Isolate / Examine Separately State C Gap / No Observation Missing row inside active operational interval No telemetry received. Indicates hardware powered off, deep sleep, app crash, power cut, or pending sync. Exclude from Uptime Baseline

docs.title: Formal Baseline Uptime Formula:
docs.text:
\[\text{Uptime } (\%) = \frac{\text{Count(State A)}}{\text{Count(State A)} + \text{Count(State B)}} \times 100\]

(Bounded strictly between 08:00 and 19:59 local device time; excludes State C gaps; isolates State D for sensitivity analysis).

docs.title: 3. Future Research & Modeling Roadmap
docs.text:
While the 4-State taxonomy provides the immediate deterministic starting point, Pillar 4 encompasses two upcoming research tracks:

  1. Measurement-Ping Validation Pipeline:

    • Construct an automated cross-validation engine that checks whether active speedtest measurement payloads exist during timeframes where ping telemetry reports downtime (State B) or gaps (State C).
    • Cross-reference startup speedtest runs (trigger_type = 'startup') upon system reboot to verify whether time-series gaps were caused by power restarts vs. ISP outages.

  2. Predictive Time-Series Disconnection Modeling:

    • Build time-series machine learning models to forecast future school offline events and predict imminent disconnections based on historical ping latency jitter, error trends, and regional outage patterns.

docs.title: Pillar 5: ISP SLA Accountability, BBR & Bufferbloat Analytics (Early Stage)
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
Standard throughput tests (download and upload speed in Mbps) fail to capture the full quality of service (QoS) experienced by end users. A school may subscribe to a 50 Mbps connection yet suffer unviable performance during digital learning sessions due to high latency under load (Bufferbloat), severe packet loss, or poor backhaul routing.

Pillar 5 exists as an exploratory research pillar to leverage kernel-level NDT7 diagnostic payloads (results JSON) to establish objective ISP Service Level Agreement (SLA) accountability.

docs.title: 2. Exploratory Research Scope & NDT7 Metrics
docs.text:
While Pillar 5 is currently in an early analytical stage, the platform extracts and maps key TCP kernel diagnostic parameters from active NDT7 test runs:

Research Metric JSON Extraction Path (results Column) Units Diagnostic & SLA Utility Download Throughput NDTResult.S2C.LastClientMeasurement.MeanClientMbps Mbps Actual user throughput during download test. Upload Throughput NDTResult.C2S.LastClientMeasurement.MeanClientMbps Mbps Actual user throughput during upload test. Working Latency (RTT) NDTResult.S2C.LastServerMeasurement.TCPInfo.RTT / 1000.0 msms Real-time round-trip latency under active load. Baseline Latency (MinRTT) NDTResult.S2C.LastServerMeasurement.BBRInfo.MinRTT / 1000.0 msms Unloaded baseline network latency. Bufferbloat (ΔRTT) RTT−MinRTT msms Latency degradation under load; identifies ISP or router queue bloat. TCP Packet Retransmissions NDTResult.S2C.LastServerMeasurement.TCPInfo.TotalRetrans Count Total retransmitted TCP packets; primary indicator of physical link loss. BBR Bottleneck Capacity NDTResult.S2C.LastServerMeasurement.BBRInfo.BW Bytes/sec The maximum end-to-end bandwidth from the server to the client as measured by BBR.

docs.title: 3. Future Analytical Direction
docs.text:
As additional diagnostic dataset assets are integrated into GigaMeter, Pillar 5 research will focus on:

  • Root-Cause Degradation Separation: Isolating whether poor user performance stems from weak local school Wi-Fi signal (wifi_signal_dbm) versus ISP backhaul congestion or inefficient M-Lab server routing.

  • Automated SLA Breach Reporting: Generating automated compliance reports comparing contractual ISP bandwidth and latency guarantees against empirical NDT7 kernel metrics.

docs.title: Pillar 1: Entity Geofencing & Mobility Trajectory Detection
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
In crowdsourced field telemetry, client monitoring software (the GigaMeter application) runs on hardware devices - such as laptops, tablets, desktop PCs, or smartphones - that are inherently susceptible to physical movement.

In real-world deployment scenarios:

  • Teachers or school staff frequently take laptops home during off-hours or weekends.

  • Hardware equipment is occasionally transferred between facilities or regional offices.

  • Users run speedtests while connected to mobile hotspots or in transit.

If telemetry from a roaming laptop is blindly assigned to a static school facility, speedtest results recorded at a teacher's home 50 kilometers away will pollute the connectivity baseline of the school building. Pillar 1 exists to evaluate hardware movement at the individual device level, separating fixed facility anchors from mobile or commuting hardware.

docs.title: 2. Core Research Objectives
docs.text:
• Isolate Device Trajectories: Track individual hardware instances (device_id / browser_id) across time and space using Density-Based Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN).

  • Disambiguate Operational Context: Differentiate between active school hours (08:00–19:59 local device time) and off-hour/weekend usage.

  • Classify Hardware Mobility Taxonomy: Categorize every registered monitoring device into one of four distinct behavioral states:

    1. STATIONARY: Dedicated fixed hardware permanently anchored to the facility campus.

    2. COMMUTER: Mobile device used at the facility during operational hours and taken home off-hours.

    3. RELOCATED: Equipment permanently transferred to another location after a specific date.

    4. HIGH_MOBILITY: Unanchored, roaming devices (e.g., field audit kits or staff smartphones).

docs.title: 3. Key Analytical Mechanics
docs.text:
• Temporal Filtering: Isolates pings and measurements recorded strictly within local device active operational hours (08:00–19:59).

  • DBSCAN Clustering: Converts coordinate pairs (detected_latitude, detected_longitude) into radians and applies DBSCAN with an 150m spatial radius threshold and min_samples = 3 density requirement.

  • Geofence Displacement Auditing: Measures instantaneous Haversine displacement (D_centroid) between individual test pings and the facility's empirical spatial anchor.

docs.title: Pillar 2: Geolocation Quality, BSSID Fingerprinting & Confidence Scoring
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text:
Crowdsourced Wi-Fi location resolution depends on ambient environmental scans submitted to Google's Geolocation API. However, field environments present significant spatial noise:

  • Facilities in rural areas may scan only 1 or 2 nearby Wi-Fi routers, yielding lower precision radii.

  • Staff frequently use consumer mobile hotspots (e.g., "iPhone", "Galaxy A15"), which move continuously across days.

  • Devices occasionally report severe BSSID spatial splits (> 2km), where a single device pings from two distant locations. Furthermore, GigaMeter operates under a Strict No-IP Fallback Policy. If Wi-Fi triangulation fails, coordinates return as NULL rather than defaulting to inaccurate ISP data centers hundreds of kilometers away. Pillar 2 exists to quantify spatial precision (0–100 score), detect mobile tethering anomalies, and apply mathematical coherence penalties to unstable hardware setups.

docs.title: 2. Core Research Objectives
docs.text:
• Inverse-Variance Spatial Weighting: Compute empirical facility centroids where high-precision scans (<= 10m) carry exponentially greater mathematical weight than low-precision scans (100m).

  • Mobile Hotspot & Drift Detection: Automatically flag personal mobile tethering via case-insensitive SSID regex matching and multi-day BSSID spatial drift checks (> 1km).

  • BSSID Coherence Penalty (P_coherence): Scale down hardware health scores when a facility's associated BSSIDs exhibit a severe spatial split (> 2km).

docs.title: 6. Key Analytical Mechanics
docs.text:
• Accuracy-Weighted Centroid Formula:
\[w_i = \frac{1}{\max(A_i, 1.0)^2}\] \[\bar{\phi} = \frac{\sum (w_i \cdot \phi_i)}{\sum w_i}, \quad \bar{\lambda} = \frac{\sum (w_i \cdot \lambda_i)}{\sum w_i}\]
  • 5-Factor Composite Scoring Model (S_raw, 0–100):
\[S_{\text{raw}} = \underbrace{S_{\text{stability}}}_{\text{30 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{consensus}}}_{\text{25 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{bssid}}}_{\text{20 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{depth}}}_{\text{15 pt}} + \underbrace{S_{\text{precision}}}_{\text{10 pt}}\]
  • BSSID Coherence Multiplier (P_coherence):
\[P_{\text{coherence}} = \begin{cases} 1.0, & \text{if } D_{\text{bssid_max}} \le 1000\text{m } \text{(Tight Alignment)} \\[1ex] 1.0 - 0.5 \times \left( \frac{D_{\text{bssid_max}} - 1000}{1000} \right), & \text{if } 1000\text{m} < D_{\text{bssid_max}} \le 2000\text{m} \\[1ex] 0.1, & \text{if } D_{\text{bssid_max}} > 2000\text{m } \text{(Severe BSSID Split)} \end{cases}\]

docs.title: Pillar 3: Government Data Validation & Administrative Map Auditing
1. Why This Pillar Exists
docs.text: National Ministries of Education and telecommunications authorities maintain master administrative registries containing official coordinates for public schools and health centers. However, these registries frequently suffer from legacy mapping errors: * School pins are often placed at the center of a village, district office, or capital city rather than on the actual school building. * Newly constructed or relocated facilities are registered with inaccurate estimated coordinates. Pillar 3 exists to cross-validate official government administrative databases against empirical, high-confidence field telemetry. Under GigaMeter Geofencing Two-Track Engine Architecture, Pillar 3 evaluates the physical building location (Track 1: Location Truth) using unpenalized spatial confidence (S_raw), ensuring that hardware anomalies (such as a laptop taken home) do not prevent valid building locations from being verified on government maps.

docs.title: 2. Core Research Objectives
docs.text:
• Empirical Displacement Calculation: Compute the Haversine distance (D_govt) between the empirical facility centroid and official government coordinates (phi_govt, lambda_govt).
  • Two-Track Engine Decoupling:
    • Track 1 (Location Truth): Evaluates building location accuracy using S_raw to emit primary location flags.
    • Track 2 (Hardware Integrity): Evaluates device deployment health using S_raw x P_coherence to emit secondary anomaly tags.
  • Actionable GIS Flag Taxonomy: Output standardized operational flags for government review:
    • VERIFIED_ACCURATE: Empirical centroid matches government registry (<= 200m) with high confidence (>= 70).
    • GOVT_PIN_MISMATCH: High-confidence telemetry proves official government pin is wrong (> 500m).
    • CAMPUS_DISPERSION: Distance is 200m–500m, reflecting a large campus, sports field, or annex.
    • UNSTABLE_MOBILE_ONLY: Telemetry confidence is < 50; requires fixed hardware deployment.

docs.title: 3. Key Analytical Mechanics
docs.text:
Decoupled Output Schema:

Facility Evaluation Payload Output (.json)
{
  "school_id_giga": "SCH_12345",
  "location_confidence_score": 82.5,
  "location_verification_flag": "VERIFIED_ACCURATE",
  "govt_displacement_m": 34.2,
  "hardware_health_score": 8.25,
  "hardware_anomaly_tags": [
    "BSSID_SPATIAL_SPLIT"
  ]
}
